source_records.title: Linear Matrix Inequalities in System and Control Theory
source_records.verification: Fresh exact source and application comparison; title page and printed pages 7, 8, 28 read; formulas on pages 7 and 8 visually checked.
locators: Chapter 2 notes, p. 28, equation (2.41), read to retain the range-condition boundary; not invoked in these strict-positive patches
source_records.source_hypotheses: Real symmetric block matrix with positive definite eliminated block R. Strict positivity of the full block is equivalent to positivity of Q-S R^{-1} S^T. The nonstrict version additionally requires S(I-RR†)=0.
source_records.dictionary: For NPK3–4, Q=Z* K Z, S=Z* K C^T, R=bar(C) K C^T; with Hermitian adjoints, Q-S R^{-1} S* is exactly Dhat. NCT uses Z_exp. IGI uses Q=G_L,S=B*,R=G_R. NIB6 uses Q=<u_r,u_r>,S=z*,R=G_<. IPR4 uses the Gram C_j* D_N C_j, eliminating the J_j block. FMG6 uses [V_0,T_0] and eliminates A_L.
source_records.application_check: The programme proves positivity/full rank and completes the complex Hermitian square at the cited sites. For fixed x, expanding ||Ex+Fη||² and replacing η by η+(F*F)^{-1}F*Ex yields the minimum x*(E*E-E*F(F*F)^{-1}F*E)x. This explicitly supplies the real-to-complex adaptation; ordinary transposes in complex-linear evaluation/conductor maps are not changed.
source_records.classification: Known classical method after the displayed Hermitian/coordinate translation; programme-specific maps and analytic bounds remain local results.
source_records.limits: No original Schur priority claim, no nonstrict theorem applied without its range condition; no assertion that Boyd et al. prove any native tail estimate.

source_records.title: Updating the Inverse of a Matrix
source_records.verification: Fresh author-hosted published copy; pp. 221–223 read, and p. 221 visually checked.
locators: p. 222, block elimination (6a)–(6b) and the immediately following determinant relation
source_records.source_hypotheses: A and I-VA^{-1}U invertible. Then (A-UV)^{-1}=A^{-1}+A^{-1}U(I-VA^{-1}U)^{-1}VA^{-1}. Finite matrices, compatible rectangular dimensions.
source_records.dictionary: IRR27: A=G_(Y,n-1), U=-z_(Y,n)*, V=z_(Y,n); I-VA^{-1}U=I_4+L_(Y,n). NPK8: A=L,U=-vhat_N*,V=vhat_N. OMR18 retains the actual original covariance/Gram and the positive rank-one denominator. PRT14 uses the finite block determinant identity with its explicit fixed frame.
source_records.application_check: Positivity of the old Gram and of I+V A^{-1}V* supplies the inverses. The minus correction follows from U=-V*. The determinant formula can also be derived directly by triangular block elimination of [A,U;V,D], as on p. 222. No floating-point conclusion is inferred.

source_records.title: Determinantal Probability Measures
source_records.verification: Fresh exact arXiv v4 dated 18 June 2003; Section 4, equation (4.1), p. 11 read and visually checked; adjoining Lemma 4.1 and Section 5 formula (5.1) read as context.
locators: Section 4, equation (4.1), p. 11 of arXiv v4
source_records.source_hypotheses: Real or complex Hilbert space with an orthonormal basis; exterior inner product defined by orthonormal ordered basis wedges. The inner product of decomposable wedges equals the determinant of pairwise inner products.
source_records.dictionary: Take both lists to be the columns of the original frame, giving ||wedge X||²=det(X*X). For NCT compare X and Bbar X with the same original quotient metric. For SGT compare X and A_(N,s)X. For PFG expand the four-column wedge in the orthonormal coordinate basis; its coefficients are the four-row minors. For MCE8 use X=[x,y].
source_records.application_check: The chosen source and image frames are the same frames already present in each local proof. Positivity and nonzero wedge follow from their stated independence. The quotient-projection and conductor transfer inequalities are proved in the programme, not imported wholesale from Lyons.

source_records.verification: Fresh publisher identity, abstract and reference 10 read; full theorem/proof body uninspected.
source_records.source_hypotheses: Real full-column-rank matrices X,Y; orthonormal QR frames Q_x,Q_y, with principal cosines represented as singular values of Q_x^T Q_y. The abstract concerns numerical stability of that algorithm.
source_records.dictionary: IF16–21 use actual Hermitian isometries U_A,U_H, cross Gram U_A*U_H=A^{-1/2}H^{1/2}, principal cosines sqrt(lambda_i), and explicitly construct the corresponding two-dimensional planes.
source_records.application_check: Only classical terminology and algorithm lineage are attributed. The complex weighted comparison and its spectrum are established by the preserved local proof, without importing real numerical stability.
